Well-structured pure-stdlib exact-Q verifier (SWAP-POLYHEDRAL-CERT-1.0) across four distinct verification modes, demonstrating fast replay (0.192-6.384 ms across 16 canonical certificates) and thorough red-team testing (62/62 adversarial forgeries rejected).

Internal consistency across text, tables, and figures: Table 1 axiom counts (1 + 3 + 14 = 18), Table 2 attack counts (12+12+12+14+12 = 62) and latencies, Fig. 1 stability ratios and Perron trace, and Fig. 2/3 numerical values all align.
strong_novelty_candidates: Zero-dependency constructive Lean 4.35.0 algebraic kernel paired with exact-rational Mercator bracketing and a 4-mode zero-float certificate auditor (SWAP-POLYHEDRAL-CERT-1.0) for Pollatos & Marchesi's [5] sub-sqrt(T) linear swap regret framework.
summary: This companion verification paper provides an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 algebraic kernel (LinearSwapRegretPolyhedral.lean) and a pure-stdlib exact-rational runtime certificate auditor (SWAP-POLYHEDRAL-CERT-1.0) targeting key algebraic and finite-instance components of Pollatos and Marchesi [5] (arXiv:2611.33081). All mathematical identities, rational Mercator brackets for log(2), RVU energy-cancellation constants, and the Student-Professor UTC-vs-trigger separation (14 vs. 20 per cycle, 3T/2 gain) presented in the PDF are internally consistent and correct. The manuscript is honest about leaving general-m Perron monotonicity, FTRL/RVU dynamics, continuous log-barrier calculus, Lemma 5's Legendre dual, and Lemma 7's recursive treeplex induction outside Lean 4. No unresolved material objections were found, though its scientific novelty and significance are bounded by its role as a finite/algebraic verification companion to [5].
weaknesses: The Lean 4 formalization is restricted to finite scalar and 2x2 algebraic invariants; the core analytic and inductive arguments of [5] (general-m adjugate Perron monotonicity, FTRL/RVU regret dynamics, continuous log-barrier calculus, Lemma 5 Legendre dual, and Lemma 7 recursive treeplex induction) remain unformalized in Lean 4.

Empirical evaluation in Modes 1-4 is limited to small-scale concrete instances (e.g., 3x3 and 4x4 matrices, small finite EFG trees), and Fig. 2(a) displays closed-form theoretical scaling curves rather than empirical FTRL play trajectories.
Table 1 omits implicit universal quantifiers and auxiliary matrix definitions in compact statement cells (e.g., Rows 11-13), requiring cross-reading with Proposition 1 and Section 3 for full context.
Minor presentation discrepancies between the PDF title and submission record title, and ambiguous 'Page 3' / '(p. 3)' cross-references to [5] on p. 4.
